keyframe_review.note: 27,862 km2 (bbox 1.73-4.73 E, 42.76-44.84 N, from Aude and the Cévennes to the Rhône). The Rouergue page gives Rouergue's land area as 9,007 km2 and says it corresponds 'roughly with the modern department of Aveyron': the shape is 3.1 times larger, beyond the factor of two. The pages opened do not say who held Gévaudan and the Lower Languedoc in 990-1065 (the Septimania page: Gothia 'fractured into smaller feudal entities' in the 10th century), nor that they were Rouergue; they may well belong to the counts of Toulouse (William IV is 'Duke of Narbonne' from 1061, Raymond IV 'count of Toulouse and Rouergue', 1096). Kept as drawn because the Toulouse ledger gains this same outline in 1066; flagged for a gap-filler: shape or label is probably wrong beyond Aveyron.

27,862 km2, the 990 outline (vertices 49 to 55). After Hugh of Rouergue's death in 1053 'his heiress Bertha contested the Rouergue with William IV of Toulouse and Raymond of Saint-Gilles'; she died in 1065, which fits the end of Cliopatria's row. The outline-versus-Aveyron discrepancy of the 990 shape applies here too.

region.text: the old County of Rouergue, of which the county of Rodez was a part; Cliopatria's outline is three times Aveyron

ledger.note: Page silent on the county's origin: 990 is Cliopatria's first year for the row. The County of Rodez page lists Richard I (died 1013/1025) as the first count of Rodez and says that county 'was formed out of part of the old County of Rouergue'; the Rouergue page has the province's capital at Rodez.

1053: Hugh of Rouergue dies and the county passes to his heiress Bertha, whom William IV of Toulouse and Raymond of Saint-Gilles contest: 'On Hugh of Rouergue's death in 1053, his heiress Bertha contested the Rouergue with William IV of Toulouse and Raymond of Saint-Gilles.' Same state, new holder.

region.text: the Rouergue after Bertha's death in 1065, taken by William IV and Raymond of Saint-Gilles of Toulouse

ledger.note: 1065: Bertha dies and the Rouergue passes to the counts of Toulouse. 'Bertha died in 1065, and William and Raymond then fought each other over the Rouergue ... an agreement recognised Raymond in the Rouergue' (undated; William IV already ruled Toulouse). Raymond IV is 'count of Toulouse and Rouergue' in the bull of 22 July 1096 and from 1094 the Rouergue was 'an appanage for the younger sons of the counts of Toulouse'. Cliopatria adds the outline to Toulouse in 1066.

wars.outcome: Bertha, Hugh of Rouergue's heiress, contested the county with William IV of Toulouse and his brother Raymond of Saint-Gilles from 1053; after her death in 1065 the brothers fought each other and an agreement (undated) recognised Raymond in the Rouergue.
wars.note: A succession dispute with no campaigns dated on the page; no contest zone is drawn in the ledger. Aveyron stands for the Rouergue proper; Cliopatria's outline is larger.

certainty.note: A feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's outline; no page gives a boundary, and the outline is three times the area of Rouergue proper.

notes:
The row is probably mislabelled or oversized: Cliopatria's County of Rouergue is 27,862 km2 reaching the Rhône (roughly Aveyron, Lozère, Hérault, Gard and Aude), while the Rouergue page gives 9,007 km2 for the province. The pages opened establish only that the old County of Rouergue (Hugh of Rouergue, d. 1053; his heiress Bertha, d. 1065) passed to the counts of Toulouse; they do not say who held the Gévaudan and the Lower Languedoc in 990-1065, and William IV was already 'Duke of Narbonne' from 1061. A gap-filler should open the 'Marquisate of Gothia' / 'Duke of Narbonne' material and decide whether the eastern 18,900 km2 belong to Toulouse from 1061 (then both this row and Toulouse's 1066 gain change).
Cliopatria's Rouergue row ends in 1065 and Toulouse takes the outline in 1066 (county-of-toulouse ledger, confidence 1); the County of Rodez page supports the year (Bertha died 1065) but dates no agreement. County of Rodez (Richard I died 1013/1025, Richard II 1050, Berengar from 1051, Richard III 1112-1135) is a lordship formed from the old county and has no Cliopatria row; no dossier is proposed. Not modelled: the Counts of Rodez after 1112, the English cession of Rouergue in 1360 (Rouergue page; see the duchy-of-aquitaine ledger), Rouergue as an appanage of Toulouse's younger sons from 1094.
Page budget: five pages were opened (budget 1-2) because the Rouergue article is a province article without history; two of them (Raymond IV, William IV) are shared with the Toulouse dossier.
